answer.rationale: The primary objective is sustained availability without losing customer writes. The three constraints are: (1) p99 write-path latency is 5x target, confined to the primary region; (2) the security patch in the current release must not be reverted; (3) settlement traffic is at peak with heavy writes. This rules out rollback_release immediately (compliance forbids it) and makes add_capacity slow relative to the urgency. route_read_replicas helps dashboard/read load but does not address write-path latency. enable_circuit_breaker would shed load but sacrifice writes during peak settlement, violating the objective of preserving customer writes. regional_failover directly addresses a primary-region-confined degradation: shifting traffic to a healthy region relieves the write path without touching the security-patched release and without dropping in-flight writes if the handoff is clean. memory_b2 documents exactly this pattern succeeding during a March regional degradation, with latency and error rates recovering within minutes. I request verification of memory_b2 to confirm the failover procedure preserved write integrity and to note any caveats about peak-traffic failover conditions. Once confirmed, the action is to execute a regional failover of the write path to the standby region, monitoring settlement queue depth and write-success rate during the transition.
